title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics + parity fixes + version bump v1.32.0
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Unify auth and retry behavior across Python/TS/Go SDKs; streaming API ergonomics improvements; parity bugfixes and compatibility updates. Bump SDK packages to v1.32.0.
description:
Motivation: We have diverging auth/retry semantics and streaming ergonomics across our Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs which leads to developer confusion and interoperability bugs. This PR unifies the core behaviors (token refresh, exponential backoff defaults, and streaming event interfaces), applies parity bugfixes discovered in QA, and bumps the SDK package versions to v1.32.0.

Changes (high level):
- Auth: centralize token refresh flow and make credential providers consistent across languages (sync/async providers where applicable). Default auth retry on 401 now attempts a single refresh+retry before surfacing error.
- Retries: standardized default retry/backoff policy (idempotent vs non-idempotent routes), moved policy definitions to shared spec and updated SDK implementations to match.
- Streaming: harmonized event callbacks/iterators: TypeScript exposes async iterator (for-of async), Python uses async generator with same event shapes, Go exposes channel-based stream with identical envelope fields. Added structured close/error events.
- Ergonomics: simplified client constructors, clearer defaults, and improved types/comments across SDKs.
- Parity fixes: fixed edge cases for partial responses and reconnect/backpressure behavior observed in perf-canary.
- Tests & examples: added cross-language smoke tests and updated quickstarts to new ergonomics.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement shared spec and apply to Python/TS/Go
- [x] Update docs/quickstarts
- [x] Add unit and integration tests
- [x] CI green and flaky tests re-run
- [x] Bump package versions and changelogs

Commit summary: 
- 7 commits: 
  - 1) spec/sdk-auth-retries-streaming: add canonical spec and examples
  - 2) python/sdk: implement auth provider parity, streaming generator, tests
  - 3) ts/sdk: add async iterator streaming adapter, retry policy refactor, typings
  - 4) go/sdk: channel stream envelope, token refresh helper, concurrency fixes
  - 5) examples: update quickstarts (python/ts/go) and docs
  - 6) tests: cross-lang smoke harness, canary integration tests
  - 7) version-bumps: bump to v1.32.0 and update changelogs

Files changed (representative):
- python/redwood_sdk/client.py: refactor auth provider, add AsyncStreamingClient wrapper
- python/tests/test_streaming_parity.py: new cross-lang smoke test
- ts/packages/redwood/src/streaming.ts: async iterator refactor, event envelope
- ts/packages/redwood/src/auth.ts: unified token refresh logic and retry shim
- go/redwood/client.go: StreamEnvelope struct, RefreshToken helper
- go/tests/integration/streaming_smoke_test.go: new smoke test harness
- docs/quickstarts/auth_retry.md: updated code samples and notes
- scripts/ci/cross_lang_smoke.sh: orchestrates cross-language smoke tests

Testing notes and CI: CI initially reported one flaky TypeScript streaming test (stream reconnect timing). I re-ran the TS job, and after adding a 50ms stabilization sleep in the harness the test stabilized. All pipelines passed afterwards (unit, lint, integration, canary). Added a follow-up TODO to replace stabilization sleep with proper backpressure signal in canary harness (ENG-8421).

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam O'Neill: Requested clearer separation of public ergonomics vs internal helpers. Suggested smaller helpers and more docstrings for Python async generator.
- Author (Ava): Split large auth helper into two smaller functions and added docstrings + examples in quickstart.
- Priya Kapoor: Asked for clarity on retry defaults for non-idempotent endpoints. We added explicit per-route override and documented it in auth_retry.md.
- Marcus Liu: Signed off after Go concurrency fixes (race-case in channel close) were addressed.

Backward compatibility / migration notes: Default behavior should be backwards-compatible for most users. The main change is that 401 now triggers a single automatic refresh+retry; clients relying on raw 401 may see different errors. Migration guidance has been added to the release notes and quickstart.

Merge outcome: Squash merge into main after all approvals. Branch removed. Packages published to internal registry and public registries: pip (1.32.0), npm (@redwood/sdk v1.32.0), go module tagged v1.32.0.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-8421: replace harness stabilization sleep with backpressure-aware signal
- PM-332: track telemetry to ensure no spike in 401 errors in production after rollout

Contact: Ava Chen (author) for any issues; triage channel #sdk-platform.
